drug_class: NMDA receptor antagonist / rapid-acting antidepressant (nasal spray)
purpose: Esketamine is used to treat depression that has not gotten better with other antidepressants, which is called treatment-resistant depression. It is also used for adults with major depression who are having thoughts of suicide or self-harm and need fast relief. It works much more quickly than most antidepressants, sometimes helping within hours or days.
how_it_works: Most antidepressants work on brain chemicals like serotonin, but esketamine works differently. It targets a receptor in the brain called NMDA, which helps restore connections between brain cells that depression can damage or weaken. Think of it like rebooting certain pathways in the brain to help lift your mood more quickly.
common_side_effects: Dizziness or feeling lightheaded, nausea, sleepiness or sedation, feeling disconnected from yourself or your surroundings (dissociation), increased blood pressure right after taking it, headache, and a spinning sensation (vertigo).
warnings: Because this medication can cause dissociation (feeling detached or 'out of it') and sedation, you must be monitored by a healthcare provider for at least 2 hours after each dose and cannot drive or operate heavy machinery on the day you take it. It is only given in a certified healthcare setting — you cannot take it home. It has a potential for misuse and dependence. Tell your doctor if you have a history of substance abuse, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or aneurysm. It should not be used during pregnancy.
typical_dosing: Esketamine is given as a nasal spray in a doctor's office or clinic — never at home. During the first month (induction), you typically use it twice a week. After that, it is usually reduced to once a week for a month, then once every one to two weeks for maintenance. Your doctor will decide the right schedule for you based on how you respond.
